# RiftLinux

> RiftLinux is the open-source Linux driver for the Oculus Rift CV1 virtual reality headset: the headset, its
> Constellation sensors and its Oculus Touch controllers, with full 6DoF head and hand tracking and room scale, for
> SteamVR games (Linux games and Windows VR games through Proton) and OpenXR applications. It is a modified Monado,
> specialized for full Rift CV1 support, installed as one package. No Windows, Oculus app, Meta account, OpenHMD or
> Room Setup is needed.

Key facts:

- Supported hardware: Oculus Rift CV1 only (not the Rift S, DK1, DK2 or Quest); Oculus Touch controllers; two
  Constellation sensors, or three for room scale (tested; the headband's rear LEDs tracked); x86-64 Linux; Vulkan
  graphics (tested on NVIDIA; AMD and Intel expected to work, not yet tested).
- Install: download the package from https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/releases (.deb for Debian/Ubuntu/Mint/Pop!_OS,
  pacman package for Arch/CachyOS/EndeavourOS/Manjaro, .rpm for Fedora, tarball for others), install it, plug in the
  Rift, start SteamVR from Steam. The package registers the SteamVR driver for every user by itself.
- First start: put the headset on, face the sensors and slowly turn the head left and right, then up and down, until
  the measuring notice goes away; then press the right Oculus button and use "Set floor" in the Rift tab.
- Tracking: Touch controllers tracked optically from every sensor; scored on the Oculus runtime's own camera frames,
  within 1-2 points of the Oculus runtime per movement. Sensors are measured from movement and placed again
  automatically when moved or knocked.
- Pairing Touch controllers without Windows: `riftlinux-setup pair` (SteamVR closed; hold Oculus + Y or Oculus + B).
- Without SteamVR: RiftLinux's own OpenXR runtime: `riftlinux-run <program>`, the app menu entry "RiftLinux Runtime",
  or right-click "Run with the Rift" (KDE) / "Open With, RiftLinux Runtime" (GNOME).
- Picture: CV1 lens distortion, true 1:1 render size, Auto-HDR, HDR games and video, motion smoothing like Oculus'
  ASW 1.0 (direct mode, the default in SteamVR).
- Desktops: X11 and Wayland (GNOME and KDE Plasma tested; on Wayland the headset is leased from the desktop).
- Help: `riftlinux-setup check` diagnoses an installation; `riftlinux-setup repair` fixes SteamVR's safe-mode block and
  similar.
- Compared with other options (October 2026): upstream Monado's CV1 driver is in no release yet and tracks the Touch
  controllers by rotation only; OpenHMD's CV1 position tracking is experimental and its controllers jitter with more
  than one sensor; ALVR and WiVRn stream to standalone headsets and do not drive a CV1.
- Licence: BSL-1.0. Author: Aditya Mehra. Not affiliated with Meta or Valve.

Website (the user guide): https://aiix.github.io/RiftLinux/

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/README.md): overview, status, comparison with other options, install, build, settings, known issues
- [User guide](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/README.md): index of the user documentation
- [Getting started](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): what you need, connecting, installing, the first start
- [FAQ](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/faq.md): does the Rift CV1 work on Linux, which driver to use, Wayland, AMD, Proton
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md): symptoms, causes and fixes; logs
- [Sensors](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/sensors.md): placing and measuring the Constellation sensors
- [Touch controllers and pairing](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/controllers.md): pairing without Windows, buttons, batteries
- [The Rift tab](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/rift-tab.md): the Oculus button menu and its settings
- [The picture](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/picture.md): direct mode, Auto-HDR, HDR, motion smoothing
- [OpenXR without SteamVR](https://github.com/AIIX/RiftLinux/blob/main/docs/openxr-without-steamvr.md): RiftLinux's own runtime, WayVR
